messages:
marta: quick heads-up — delta7b int8 smoke tests are in. big unit-econ win but we saw a measurable quality hit on longform summarization slices. sharing numbers + thinking about routing/playbook. :thinking:
ryan: paste the numbers when you have them?
marta: here are the summary results from sparkbench + manual eval (slice: longform-summ):
```
SparkBench: delta7b fp16 vs int8 (single GPU, same batch config)
slice: longform-summ (avg input 820 tokens)
- p95 latency: fp16 180ms  |  int8 210ms
- tokens/second (inference): fp16 1.02  |  int8 0.45
- cost per 1k tokens: fp16 $0.0075  |  int8 $0.0032
- manual recall@k (golded): fp16 76.6%  |  int8 72.1%  (delta -4.5pp)
- ROUGE-L drop (avg): ~3.8 pts
- sample size: 600 dialogs, stratified by length
- note: int8 shows more failure modes on long context priming (hallucination-ish)
```
link: https://internal.redwood/sparkbench/delta7b/3099998887
ryan: econ quick take — ~2.3x cheaper on token cost. for a 1M token-month workload that's roughly $3.2k vs $7.5k -> ~ $4.3k/mo savings at model-level. but product impact could swamp that if retention/ltv affected.
devin: two practical ideas: 1) hybrid routing based on token length & novelty score, 2) small canary w/ fallback to fp16 on quality trigger. example routing rule: 
```
# simple pseudo-rule
if request.tokens > 512 or novelty_score < 0.6:
    route -> delta7b-fp16
else:
    route -> delta7b-int8
```
sophia: quick product question — how many requests fall into that longform bucket? if it's tiny maybe we default to int8 and accept small hit.
marta: longform-summ is ~12% of requests but accounts for ~28% of retention-sensitive flows (onboarding summaries, weekly digests). so not tiny. recommend conservative approach.
devin: additional ops levers: prefix/KV caching for long contexts reduces fp16 cost by ~25-35% in prior tests; we can combine caching + hybrid routing to recover some econ. also consider softer quant (int6 for short) if model supports.
ryan: for GTN/product decks we should prepare: unit-econ delta, projected revenue sensitivity (if recall drops 1pt -> x% churn), and fallback cost. i'll draft slide.
marta: proposed rollout: 1) create 5% canary (int8 default for all, route longform 5% -> fp16), 2) collect quality signals (recall, rouge, hallucination heuristic) for 72h, 3) auto-fallback policy if quality delta exceeds threshold for 6h.
devin: fallback pseudo-policy: 
```
quality_window = 6h
if quality_delta(fp16,int8) > 2.0 pts over quality_window:
    route_all_longform -> fp16
    notify(#product, #eng-ml)
```
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary job created: delta7b-int8-canary @ 5% longform -> delta7b-fp16 fallback enabled. See: https://internal.redwood/deploys/3099998887
sophia: ack — will loop in GTN on sensitivity numbers once ryan posts slide.
marta: next steps: i) run 72h canary + collect automated eval hooks ii) ryan to complete unit-econ slide iii) devin to add caching config suggestion to the playbook. i'll post interim results in this thread. :thumbsup:
